- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of forecast before final output.
- In early horizon (e.g., 1–5 days ahead), model tends to be too optimistic; apply 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often fails to adjust; force forecast to align with 30-day moving average of past 10 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment weight to forecast adjustment.
